newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks end up, shift to medium caps seen.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks end up, shift to medium caps seen.

text.p: Greek stocks ended up 1.26 percent on Tuesday after a short-lived correction early in the session with analysts saying intra-day corrections were the result of portfolio reallocation from large to medium cap stocks.
"The session started lower but quickly rebounded on two or three large orders for OTE and National Bank," said John Tegopoulos, an analyst at Midland Pantelakis Securities.
A shift from large to medium capitalisation stocks started on Friday, Tegopoulos said.
The investment public starts focusing now on medium capitalisation stocks which do not weigh much on the general index and this explains why the index trades lower, he added.
The market should consolidate at 1,130 to 1,170 points this week, he said.
Medium capitalisation food companies Goody's and Chipita were attractive stocks because their P/E was lower than the market's and enjoyed good earnings growth, he said.
Metallurgical firm METKA and Silver and baryte Ores were also attractive interms of P/E, he added.
Rallies in blue chips were cyclical and would be repeated in 1997, said Tegopoulos.
Other analysts said the market would likely face intra-day corrections in the following sessions until Friday.
"Corrections will take place during the course of the next few sessions but the general share index will manage to close higher", said George Politis, an analyst at Eurosec Securities.
These corrections originate from portfolio restructuring towards medium capitalisation stocks and away from blue chips, he said.
The Athens general share index closed 1.26 percent or 14.48 points up at 1162.54 from Monday's 1148.06, after opening at 1144.73.
Politis expected the index to close at 1,180 points at the end of the week.

Tuesday's turnover was slightly lower at 15.2 billion drachmas on volume of 4.9 million shares, with block trades of Alpha Credit and Titan TTNr.AT shares. Gainers led losers 120 to 90 with 28 issues unchanged on 238 traded.
Leasing shares led with a rise of 2.41 and bank shares ended 1.36 percent higher.
Leasing shares are cheap and therefore attractive to the market, Politis said.
Construction shares lost 1.43 percent while industrials gained 0.42 percent. Investment shares slipped 0.28 percent and industrials rose 0.42 perccent while small caps ended 0.27 percent up.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted higher at 900.00-918.00. Shares of OTE telecom the underlying, climbed 230 drachmas to close at 5,365.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $21.37-$22.37. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted higher at 8,074-8,558 drachmas.

On Monday, the Greek Finance Ministry auctioned 300 billion drachmas of 12-month T-bills. The average accepted price stood at 90.15 and the cutoff price at 90.04. Another 90 billion drachmas of 12-month T-bills were allocated in non-competitive bids.
--Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
